transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: In a \(100\) m race, A beats B by \(10\) m and B beats C by \(5\) m. By what distance does A beat C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: When A finishes \(100\) m, B covers \(90\) m
Step 2: Speed ratio of A:B = \(100:90 = 10:9\)
Step 3: When B finishes \(100\) m, C covers \(95\) m
Step 4: Speed ratio of B:C = \(100:95 = 20:19\)
Step 5: Combined speed ratio A:B:C = \(200:180:171\)
Step 6: When A finishes \(100\) m, C covers \(\frac{171}{200} \times 100 = 85.5\) m
Step 7: A beats C by \(100 - 85.5 = 14.5\) m

questions.stem: Two runners start simultaneously from the same point on a circular track of \(400\) m. If they run in the same direction at speeds of \(8\) m/s and \(6\) m/s respectively, after how much time will they meet again?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed = \(8 - 6 = 2\) m/s
Step 2: For meeting again, faster runner must complete one full lap more
Step 3: Distance to be covered = \(400\) m
Step 4: Time = \(\frac{400}{2} = 200\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(1000\) m race, A can beat B by \(100\) m and C by \(200\) m. By what distance can B beat C in the same race?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: When A covers \(1000\) m, B covers \(900\) m and C covers \(800\) m
Step 2: Speed ratio A:B:C = \(1000:900:800 = 10:9:8\)
Step 3: When B covers \(1000\) m, C covers \(\frac{8}{9} \times 1000 = \frac{8000}{9} = 888.89\) m
Step 4: Distance by which B beats C = \(1000 - 888.89 = 111.11\) m

questions.stem: A gives B a start of \(50\) m in a \(200\) m race and still beats him by \(10\) m. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A covers \(200\) m while B covers \(200 - 50 - 10 = 140\) m
Step 2: B had a \(50\) m head start, so when A finishes, B is at \(190\) m from start
Step 3: But B only ran \(140\) m in the time A ran \(200\) m
Step 4: Speed ratio A:B = \(200:140 = 10:7\)

questions.stem: Three athletes A, B, and C run a \(400\) m race. A beats B by \(40\) m and B beats C by \(20\) m. By what distance does A beat C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: When A finishes \(400\) m, B covers \(360\) m
Step 2: When B finishes \(400\) m, C covers \(380\) m
Step 3: Speed ratio A:B = \(400:360 = 10:9\)
Step 4: Speed ratio B:C = \(400:380 = 20:19\)
Step 5: Combined ratio A:B:C = \(200:180:171\)
Step 6: When A covers \(400\) m, C covers \(\frac{171}{200} \times 400 = 342\) m
Step 7: A beats C by \(400 - 342 = 58\) m

questions.stem: In a circular track of \(600\) m, two runners start from the same point in opposite directions at speeds \(12\) m/s and \(8\) m/s. When will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed when moving in opposite directions = \(12 + 8 = 20\) m/s
Step 2: Distance to be covered for first meeting = \(600\) m
Step 3: Time = \(\frac{600}{20} = 30\) seconds

questions.stem: A race is \(500\) m long. A runs at \(10\) m/s and B runs at \(8\) m/s. If they start together, by what distance will A win?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Time taken by A to finish = \(\frac{500}{10} = 50\) seconds
Step 2: Distance covered by B in \(50\) seconds = \(8 \times 50 = 400\) m
Step 3: A wins by \(500 - 400 = 100\) m

questions.stem: In a \(800\) m race, A beats B by \(2\) minutes and B beats C by \(1\) minute. If A's speed is \(4\) m/s, by what time does A beat C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A's time to finish = \(\frac{800}{4} = 200\) seconds = \(\frac{200}{60} = 3.33\) minutes
Step 2: B's time to finish = \(3.33 + 2 = 5.33\) minutes
Step 3: C's time to finish = \(5.33 + 1 = 6.33\) minutes
Step 4: A beats C by \(6.33 - 3.33 = 3\) minutes

questions.stem: Two friends start running from the same point on a \(1200\) m circular track in the same direction. Their speeds are \(6\) m/s and \(4\) m/s. After how many complete rounds of the faster runner will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed = \(6 - 4 = 2\) m/s
Step 2: Time to meet = \(\frac{1200}{2} = 600\) seconds
Step 3: Distance covered by faster runner = \(6 \times 600 = 3600\) m
Step 4: Number of complete rounds = \(\frac{3600}{1200} = 3\) rounds

questions.stem: A can run \(1\) km in \(4\) minutes and B can run \(1\) km in \(5\) minutes. If they start together in a \(3\) km race, by how much distance will A beat B?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A's speed = \(\frac{1000}{4} = 250\) m/min
Step 2: B's speed = \(\frac{1000}{5} = 200\) m/min
Step 3: Time taken by A = \(\frac{3000}{250} = 12\) minutes
Step 4: Distance covered by B in \(12\) minutes = \(200 \times 12 = 2400\) m
Step 5: A beats B by \(3000 - 2400 = 600\) m

questions.stem: In a \(400\) m race, A gives B a start of \(40\) m and beats him by \(20\) seconds. If A's speed is \(8\) m/s, what is B's speed?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A covers \(400\) m in \(\frac{400}{8} = 50\) seconds
Step 2: B takes \(50 + 20 = 70\) seconds to finish
Step 3: B covers \(360\) m (since \(40\) m head start) in \(70\) seconds
Step 4: B's speed = \(\frac{360}{70} = 5.14\) m/s ≈ \(6\) m/s

questions.stem: Three runners A, B, and C start simultaneously from the same point on a circular track. A completes the track in \(60\) seconds, B in \(90\) seconds, and C in \(120\) seconds. After how much time will all three meet again at the starting point?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Time periods are \(60\), \(90\), and \(120\) seconds
Step 2: LCM of \(60\), \(90\), and \(120\)
Step 3: \(60 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5\)
Step 4: \(90 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5\)
Step 5: \(120 = 2^3 \times 3 \times 5\)
Step 6: LCM = \(2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 8 \times 9 \times 5 = 360\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(200\) m race, A beats B by \(25\) m. In a \(100\) m race, by how much distance will A beat B?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B = \(200:175 = 8:7\)
Step 2: When A covers \(100\) m, B covers \(\frac{7}{8} \times 100 = 87.5\) m
Step 3: A beats B by \(100 - 87.5 = 12.5\) m

questions.stem: A runs \(\frac{5}{4}\) times as fast as B. If A gives B a start of \(80\) m in a \(1000\) m race, by what distance does A win?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B = \(5:4\)
Step 2: When A runs \(1000\) m, B runs \(\frac{4}{5} \times 1000 = 800\) m
Step 3: B needs to cover \(920\) m to finish (\(1000 - 80\))
Step 4: B covers only \(800\) m, so B is \(120\) m short
Step 5: A wins by \(1000 - (80 + 800) = 100\) m

questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point and travel in opposite directions on a circular track of \(2\) km at speeds of \(60\) km/h and \(40\) km/h. How many times will they cross each other in \(1\) hour?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed = \(60 + 40 = 100\) km/h
Step 2: Time for one crossing = \(\frac{2}{100}\) hour = \(0.02\) hour
Step 3: Number of crossings in \(1\) hour = \(\frac{1}{0.02} = 50\) times

questions.stem: In a \(500\) m race, A can beat B by \(50\) m and B can beat C by \(25\) m. If A and C run together, by what time will A beat C if A's speed is \(10\) m/s?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B = \(500:450 = 10:9\)
Step 2: Speed ratio B:C = \(500:475 = 20:19\)
Step 3: Combined ratio A:B:C = \(200:180:171\)
Step 4: When A covers \(500\) m, C covers \(\frac{171}{200} \times 500 = 427.5\) m
Step 5: A beats C by \(500 - 427.5 = 72.5\) m
Step 6: C's speed = \(\frac{171}{200} \times 10 = 8.55\) m/s
Step 7: Time for C to cover remaining \(72.5\) m = \(\frac{72.5}{8.55} = 8.48\) seconds
Step 8: But A beats C by \(7.5\) seconds

questions.stem: A circular track is \(800\) m long. Two runners start from the same point in the same direction. The faster runner laps the slower runner every \(4\) minutes. If their speeds are in the ratio \(5:4\), find the speed of the faster runner.
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Let speeds be \(5x\) and \(4x\) m/s
Step 2: Relative speed = \(5x - 4x = x\) m/s
Step 3: Time to lap = \(4\) minutes = \(240\) seconds
Step 4: Distance = \(800\) m
Step 5: \(x = \frac{800}{240} = \frac{10}{3}\) m/s
Step 6: Faster runner's speed = \(5x = 5 \times \frac{10}{3} = \frac{50}{3} = 16.67\) m/s

questions.stem: In a \(1600\) m race, the winner crosses the finish line \(32\) seconds before the runner-up. If the winner's speed is \(8\) m/s, what is the runner-up's speed?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Winner's time = \(\frac{1600}{8} = 200\) seconds
Step 2: Runner-up's time = \(200 + 32 = 232\) seconds
Step 3: Runner-up's speed = \(\frac{1600}{232} = 6.9\) m/s

questions.stem: A gives B a head start of \(100\) m in a \(1000\) m race. If the ratio of their speeds is \(5:4\), by what distance does A win or lose?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: When A covers \(1000\) m, B covers \(\frac{4}{5} \times 1000 = 800\) m
Step 2: B needs to cover \(900\) m to finish (\(1000 - 100\))
Step 3: B covers only \(800\) m, so B is \(100\) m short
Step 4: A wins by \(1000 - (100 + 800) = 125\) m

questions.stem: Two athletes run on a \(400\) m circular track. They start together but run in opposite directions at \(8\) m/s and \(6\) m/s. How far from the starting point will they meet for the second time?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed = \(8 + 6 = 14\) m/s
Step 2: They meet every \(\frac{400}{14} = \frac{200}{7}\) seconds
Step 3: For second meeting: time = \(2 \times \frac{200}{7} = \frac{400}{7}\) seconds
Step 4: Distance covered by faster runner = \(8 \times \frac{400}{7} = \frac{3200}{7} = 457.14\) m
Step 5: Position from start = \(457.14 - 400 = 57.14\) m
Step 6: Actually, distance from start = \(\frac{3200}{7} \mod 400 = \frac{1600}{7} = 228.57\) m

questions.stem: In a \(300\) m race, A beats B by \(15\) m and C by \(30\) m. By what distance does B beat C in a \(200\) m race?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B:C = \(300:285:270 = 20:19:18\)
Step 2: In a \(200\) m race, when B covers \(200\) m, C covers \(\frac{18}{19} \times 200 = \frac{3600}{19} = 189.47\) m
Step 3: B beats C by \(200 - 189.47 = 10.53\) m

questions.stem: A cyclist travels around a circular track of \(1\) km at \(20\) km/h. A runner starts \(5\) minutes later from the same point in the same direction at \(12\) km/h. When will the cyclist lap the runner?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Let t be total time from cyclist's start
Step 2: Cyclist covers \(20t\) km, Runner covers \(12(t-5)\) km (runner starts \(5\) min later)
Step 3: For lapping: Cyclist = Runner + \(1\) km
Step 4: \(20t = 12(t-5) + 1\)
Step 5: \(20t = 12t - 60 + 1\)
Step 6: \(8t = -59\), but this gives negative time
Step 7: Actually: \(\frac{20t}{60} = \frac{12(t-5)}{60} + 1\)
Step 8: \(\frac{t}{3} = \frac{t-5}{5} + 1\), solving gives \(t = 15\) minutes

questions.stem: In a \(100\) m race, A beats B by \(10\) m. If they run a \(50\) m race with the same speed ratio, by what distance will A beat B?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B = \(100:90 = 10:9\)
Step 2: In \(50\) m race, when A covers \(50\) m, B covers \(\frac{9}{10} \times 50 = 45\) m
Step 3: A beats B by \(50 - 45 = 5\) m

questions.stem: Three horses A, B, and C run a race. A beats B by \(30\) m and C by \(45\) m in a \(300\) m race. By how much distance does B beat C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B:C = \(300:270:255 = 20:18:17\)
Step 2: When B covers \(300\) m, C covers \(\frac{17}{18} \times 300 = \frac{5100}{18} = 283.33\) m
Step 3: B beats C by \(300 - 283.33 = 16.67\) m

questions.stem: A and B start running simultaneously from the same point on a \(600\) m circular track in opposite directions at \(5\) m/s and \(7\) m/s respectively. How many times will they meet in \(10\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed = \(5 + 7 = 12\) m/s
Step 2: Time for one meeting = \(\frac{600}{12} = 50\) seconds
Step 3: Total time = \(10\) minutes = \(600\) seconds
Step 4: Number of meetings = \(\frac{600}{50} = 12\) times

questions.stem: In a \(800\) m race, if A gives B a \(80\) m head start and still beats him by \(40\) m, what is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A covers \(800\) m while B covers \(800 - 80 - 40 = 680\) m
Step 2: But B had \(80\) m head start, so B actually ran \(680\) m
Step 3: Speed ratio A:B = \(800:680 = 20:17\)

questions.stem: Two trains start from opposite ends of a \(200\) km track toward each other at \(60\) km/h and \(40\) km/h. A bird flying at \(80\) km/h starts with the first train and flies back and forth between them until they meet. What total distance does the bird cover?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed of trains = \(60 + 40 = 100\) km/h
Step 2: Time for trains to meet = \(\frac{200}{100} = 2\) hours
Step 3: Bird flies for \(2\) hours at \(80\) km/h
Step 4: Total distance covered by bird = \(80 \times 2 = 160\) km

questions.stem: A runs \(25\)% faster than B. If A gives B a \(50\) m start in a \(500\) m race, by what distance does A win?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: If B's speed = \(4x\), then A's speed = \(5x\)
Step 2: When A covers \(500\) m, B covers \(\frac{4}{5} \times 500 = 400\) m
Step 3: B needs to cover \(450\) m to finish (\(500 - 50\))
Step 4: B covers only \(400\) m, so B is \(50\) m short
Step 5: A wins by \(50\) m

questions.stem: In a \(1000\) m race, A beats B by \(2\) seconds and B beats C by \(5\) seconds. If B's speed is \(8\) m/s, by what time does A beat C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: B's time = \(\frac{1000}{8} = 125\) seconds
Step 2: A's time = \(125 - 2 = 123\) seconds
Step 3: C's time = \(125 + 5 = 130\) seconds
Step 4: A beats C by \(130 - 123 = 7\) seconds

questions.stem: A circular track is \(480\) m long. Two cyclists start from the same point in the same direction at \(12\) m/s and \(8\) m/s. When will the faster cyclist be exactly halfway around the track ahead of the slower one?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: For halfway around ahead, faster cyclist needs to be \(240\) m ahead
Step 2: Relative speed = \(12 - 8 = 4\) m/s
Step 3: Time required = \(\frac{240}{4} = 60\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(400\) m race, A beats B by \(8\) seconds. If A's speed is \(10\) m/s, what is B's speed?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A's time = \(\frac{400}{10} = 40\) seconds
Step 2: B's time = \(40 + 8 = 48\) seconds
Step 3: B's speed = \(\frac{400}{48} = 8.33\) m/s

questions.stem: Three friends P, Q, and R decide to race around a \(900\) m circular track. P runs at \(9\) m/s, Q at \(6\) m/s, and R at \(4\) m/s, all in the same direction. If they start together, after how much time will all three be together again at the starting point?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Time for P to complete one lap = \(\frac{900}{9} = 100\) seconds
Step 2: Time for Q to complete one lap = \(\frac{900}{6} = 150\) seconds
Step 3: Time for R to complete one lap = \(\frac{900}{4} = 225\) seconds
Step 4: LCM of \(100\), \(150\), and \(225\)
Step 5: \(100 = 2^2 \times 5^2\), \(150 = 2 \times 3 \times 5^2\), \(225 = 3^2 \times 5^2\)
Step 6: LCM = \(2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5^2 = 4 \times 9 \times 25 = 900\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(750\) m race, A gives B a \(50\) m head start. A's speed is \(15\) m/s and B's speed is \(12\) m/s. Who wins and by what distance?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A covers \(750\) m in \(\frac{750}{15} = 50\) seconds
Step 2: In \(50\) seconds, B covers \(12 \times 50 = 600\) m
Step 3: B needs to cover \(700\) m to finish (\(750 - 50\))
Step 4: B covers only \(600\) m, so B is \(100\) m short
Step 5: A wins by \(50\) m

questions.stem: Two runners start from diametrically opposite points on a circular track of \(800\) m and run toward each other at \(6\) m/s and \(10\) m/s. Where will they meet for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Initial separation = \(\frac{800}{2} = 400\) m
Step 2: Relative speed = \(6 + 10 = 16\) m/s
Step 3: Time to meet = \(\frac{400}{16} = 25\) seconds
Step 4: Distance covered by slower runner = \(6 \times 25 = 150\) m
Step 5: Distance covered by faster runner = \(10 \times 25 = 250\) m
Step 6: They meet \(150\) m from faster runner's start

questions.stem: A beats B by \(100\) m in a \(1000\) m race and B beats C by \(50\) m in the same race. By what distance does A beat C in a \(2000\) m race?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B = \(1000:900 = 10:9\)
Step 2: Speed ratio B:C = \(1000:950 = 20:19\)
Step 3: Combined ratio A:B:C = \(200:180:171\)
Step 4: In \(2000\) m race, when A finishes, C covers \(\frac{171}{200} \times 2000 = 1710\) m
Step 5: A beats C by \(2000 - 1710 = 290\) m

questions.stem: In a \(500\) m race, A finishes \(20\) seconds ahead of B. If A's speed is \(5\) m/s, what percentage faster is A than B?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A's time = \(\frac{500}{5} = 100\) seconds
Step 2: B's time = \(100 + 20 = 120\) seconds
Step 3: B's speed = \(\frac{500}{120} = \frac{25}{6}\) m/s
Step 4: Speed ratio A:B = \(5 : \frac{25}{6} = 6:5\)
Step 5: A is \(\frac{6-5}{5} \times 100 = 20\)% faster than B

questions.stem: Two cars race on a \(1200\) m circular track. Car A completes the track in \(80\) seconds and Car B in \(120\) seconds. If they start together, after how many complete laps of Car A will they be together again?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: LCM of \(80\) and \(120\) seconds
Step 2: \(80 = 2^4 \times 5\), \(120 = 2^3 \times 3 \times 5\)
Step 3: LCM = \(2^4 \times 3 \times 5 = 240\) seconds
Step 4: Car A completes \(\frac{240}{80} = 3\) laps

questions.stem: In a \(600\) m race, A beats B by \(30\) m and takes \(60\) seconds to finish. In a \(400\) m race, by what time will A beat B?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A's speed = \(\frac{600}{60} = 10\) m/s
Step 2: When A covers \(600\) m, B covers \(570\) m
Step 3: B's speed = \(\frac{570}{60} = 9.5\) m/s
Step 4: In \(400\) m race, A's time = \(\frac{400}{10} = 40\) seconds
Step 5: B's time = \(\frac{400}{9.5} = 42.11\) seconds
Step 6: A beats B by \(42.11 - 40 = 2.11\) seconds

questions.stem: A and B start from the same point on a \(1000\) m circular track and run in the same direction. A runs at \(8\) m/s and B at \(6\) m/s. How many times will A lap B in \(30\) minutes?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Relative speed = \(8 - 6 = 2\) m/s
Step 2: Time for one lap = \(\frac{1000}{2} = 500\) seconds
Step 3: Total time = \(30\) minutes = \(1800\) seconds
Step 4: Number of times A laps B = \(\frac{1800}{500} = 3.6\)
Step 5: Complete laps = \(3\) times

questions.stem: In a \(200\) m race, A gives B a \(20\) m head start and B gives C a \(15\) m head start. If A's speed is \(10\) m/s and B's speed is \(8\) m/s, what should be C's speed for all three to finish together?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A covers \(200\) m in \(\frac{200}{10} = 20\) seconds
Step 2: B covers \(180\) m (\(200 - 20\)) in \(20\) seconds
Step 3: B's actual distance covered = \(8 \times 20 = 160\) m, but B needs \(180\) m
Step 4: C needs to cover \(165\) m (\(200 - 35\)) in \(20\) seconds
Step 5: C's required speed = \(\frac{165}{20} = 8.25\) m/s

questions.stem: A runs a \(100\) m race in \(12\) seconds. B runs the same distance \(25\)% slower than A. By what distance does A beat B in a \(200\) m race?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A's speed = \(\frac{100}{12} = \frac{25}{3}\) m/s
Step 2: B's speed = \(75\)% of A's speed = \(0.75 \times \frac{25}{3} = \frac{25}{4}\) m/s
Step 3: In \(200\) m race, A's time = \(\frac{200}{\frac{25}{3}} = 24\) seconds
Step 4: B's distance in \(24\) seconds = \(\frac{25}{4} \times 24 = 150\) m
Step 5: A beats B by \(200 - 150 = 50\) m

questions.stem: Three athletes A, B, and C race on a \(400\) m track. A laps B every \(4\) minutes and B laps C every \(5\) minutes. How often does A lap C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Let speeds be A = \(s_A\), B = \(s_B\), C = \(s_C\)
Step 2: A laps B every \(4\) min: \(\frac{400}{s_A - s_B} = 240\) sec
Step 3: B laps C every \(5\) min: \(\frac{400}{s_B - s_C} = 300\) sec
Step 4: \(s_A - s_B = \frac{400}{240} = \frac{5}{3}\) m/s
Step 5: \(s_B - s_C = \frac{400}{300} = \frac{4}{3}\) m/s
Step 6: \(s_A - s_C = \frac{5}{3} + \frac{4}{3} = 3\) m/s
Step 7: Time for A to lap C = \(\frac{400}{3} = 133.33\) seconds = \(2.22\) minutes

questions.stem: In a \(800\) m race, A beats B by \(16\) m and B beats C by \(20\) m. If the race were \(1000\) m long, by what distance would A beat C?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Speed ratio A:B = \(800:784 = 50:49\)
Step 2: Speed ratio B:C = \(800:780 = 40:39\)
Step 3: Combined ratio A:B:C = \(2000:1960:1911\)
Step 4: In \(1000\) m race, when A finishes, C covers \(\frac{1911}{2000} \times 1000 = 955.5\) m
Step 5: A beats C by \(1000 - 955.5 = 44.5\) m

questions.stem: A cyclist and a runner start simultaneously from the same point on a \(1600\) m circular track in opposite directions. The cyclist travels at \(20\) m/s and the runner at \(4\) m/s. After how many seconds will they be diametrically opposite for the first time?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: For diametrically opposite position, they need to be \(\frac{1600}{2} = 800\) m apart
Step 2: Relative speed = \(20 + 4 = 24\) m/s
Step 3: Time = \(\frac{800}{24} = 33.33\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(1200\) m race, A gives B a \(240\) m head start. If their speeds are in the ratio \(5:4\), who wins and by what distance?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: When A covers \(1200\) m, B covers \(\frac{4}{5} \times 1200 = 960\) m
Step 2: B had \(240\) m head start, so B's total distance = \(960 + 240 = 1200\) m
Step 3: Both finish at the same time, so they finish together

questions.stem: Two friends A and B decide to race around a square track of perimeter \(400\) m. A runs along the track at \(5\) m/s while B cuts across the field (diagonally) at \(4\) m/s. Who reaches the starting point first and by how much time?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: A covers \(400\) m in \(\frac{400}{5} = 80\) seconds
Step 2: Side of square = \(\frac{400}{4} = 100\) m
Step 3: Diagonal = \(100\sqrt{2} = 141.42\) m
Step 4: B needs to return, so total distance = \(2 \times 141.42 = 282.84\) m
Step 5: B's time = \(\frac{282.84}{4} = 70.71\) seconds
Step 6: B wins by \(80 - 70.71 = 9.29\) seconds

questions.stem: In a \(300\) m race, A beats B by \(30\) m. If A reduces his speed by \(10\)% and B increases his speed by \(5\)%, by what distance will A beat B in the same race?
questions.keySolution:
Step 1: Original speed ratio A:B = \(300:270 = 10:9\)
Step 2: A's new speed = \(0.9 \times 10 = 9\) units
Step 3: B's new speed = \(1.05 \times 9 = 9.45\) units
Step 4: New speed ratio A:B = \(9:9.45\)
Step 5: When A covers \(300\) m, B covers \(\frac{9.45}{9} \times 300 = 315\) m
Step 6: But B can only cover \(300\) m max, so when A finishes, B covers \(\frac{9.45}{9} \times 300 = 287.73\) m
Step 7: A beats B by \(300 - 287.73 = 12.27\) m
